title: Contesting, DX, logs and remote operation
blurb: Explain split DX operating, where contests happen, what ADIF, Cabrillo and LoTW do, remote-operation identification, latency and mesh networks.

E2C01.why: With the remote transmitter in the US you ID normally: **no additional indicator** is required.
E2C01.trap: State, district and section suffixes are not required here.

E2C02.why: **ADIF** is the standard file format for exchanging amateur log data between programs.
E2C02.trap: Cabrillo is for contest submissions, not general log exchange.

E2C03.why: Contests are generally **excluded from 30 m** (a WARC band). 6 m, 70 cm and 33 cm all host contests.

E2C04.why: Mesh networks use **frequencies shared with unlicensed wireless data services**, because they run on Wi-Fi style hardware.

E2C05.why: A QSL manager **receives and sends confirmations** on behalf of a DX station.
E2C05.trap: It doesn't run nets or allocate frequencies.

E2C06.why: VHF/UHF SSB and CW activity gathers in the **weak-signal segment, near the calling frequency**.

E2C07.why: **Cabrillo** is the standard format for submitting electronic contest logs.
E2C07.trap: It isn't the exchange sent on the air or a digital mode.

E2C08.why: LoTW confirms special event, US to non-US and Worked All States contacts: **all of these**.

E2C09.why: Mesh nodes are **wireless routers running custom firmware**.
E2C09.trap: TNC radios and EchoLink are different systems.

E2C10.why: Split operation separates callers from the DX, reduces interference, and avoids frequencies some callers can't use: **all of these**.

E2C11.why: In a pileup keep it short: your **full call sign, once or twice**.
E2C11.trap: Partial calls and long phrases waste time and add to the pileup.

E2C12.why: The delay from a control operator's action to the signal change is **latency**.
E2C12.trap: Hang time is the delay before the radio returns to receive.
